[CI]: bootstrap pip on self-hosted coverage upload runners (#23020)

Self-hosted linux-amd64-cpu-2-hk runners have python3 but no pip on PATH
after #22476. Install regex, pyyaml, and esdk-obs-python via get-pip.py
and python3 -m pip. Trigger schedule_test_coverage on pull_request so
the upload path can be verified.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

### How was this patch tested?

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

commits.message:
[Doc][Misc] Document Ascend Docker Runtime container setup (#21712)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Every model tutorial's **4.1 Docker Image Installation** section spells
out each NPU device node (`--device /dev/davinci0` … up to 16 lines on
A3) and the driver mounts (`/usr/local/dcmi`, `/usr/local/bin/npu-smi`,
`/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64`). The same block is repeated in 27
pages, and the only differences between A2, A3, and 950DT Products are
the image tag, the number of DIE devices, and a few host files.

This PR makes Ascend Docker Runtime the container form used by the
tutorials and documents it in the installation guide.

**Installation guide (`getting_started/installation.md`)**

- The install and verification steps now live in **Set up the software
environment > Use Ascend Docker Runtime**, above the three installation
paths, because both container paths (prebuilt image and CANN
environment) need it on the host.
- Install and verify: `chmod u+x`, `.run --install` as root, `systemctl
daemon-reload && systemctl restart docker`, and a `docker info --format`
check for `default=ascend`, including the `--runtime ascend` and
`daemon.json` fallbacks when it prints `runc`.
- Custom mounts through `ASCEND_RUNTIME_MOUNTS`: the value **replaces**
the default set, so `base` has to be listed explicitly
(`base,hostextra`); `base.list` is no longer edited by hand.
- **Additional guides > Manual device mapping without Ascend Docker
Runtime**: the explicit device and driver flags for Atlas A2, Atlas A3,
950DT products, Atlas 300I DUO, and Atlas 200I Pro, for hosts that
choose not to install the runtime. The runtime instructions, the shared
fragment, and the Quick Start page link to it.

**Tutorials (27 pages)**

- Each container section now opens with one shared note: it says the
commands need Ascend Docker Runtime on the host, what the runtime
mounts, that the guide assumes 26.3.0 or later, and where the manual
device mapping fallback is. The note lives in one fragment,
`getting_started/installation/ascend_docker_runtime.inc.md`, included by
the 27 tutorial pages, so it cannot drift apart.
- Each "Docker Image Installation" section drops the device and driver
flags and selects the NPUs with `ASCEND_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (A2 `0-7`, A3
`0-15`, 950DT `0-7`, Atlas 300I DUO `0-7` or `0`, Atlas 200I Pro `0`),
keeping the product-specific mounts, weight and cache directories, and
container options.
- The values keep the device counts of the removed `--device` lines, so
a page that used one NPU still selects one ID.
- Later chapters that start a second container with SSD or MemCache
devices keep their explicit flags; they do not set
`ASCEND_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, so they work with or without the runtime
installed.

Net diff: 55 files, +454 / -1777; the 27 tutorial pages drop 1,375
lines, almost all of them per-device lines and driver mounts.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Documentation only, so no release note fragment is required.

### How was this patch tested?

- `mkdocs build --strict` on this branch: builds cleanly, the new
section and all 27 tutorial pages render (including tabbed code blocks),
and the tutorial links resolve to
`installation.html#installation-ascend-docker-runtime`.
- Behavior claims checked against the Ascend-docker-runtime 26.1.0 run
package:
- `run_main.sh`: the installer requires root, accepts
`--install-scene=docker|containerd|isula` (`crio` only in newer
releases), and writes `/etc/ascend-docker-runtime.d/base.list`.
- `base.list`: `/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64`,
`/usr/local/Ascend/driver/include`, `/usr/local/dcmi`,
`/usr/local/bin/npu-smi`, `/var/queue_schedule`.
- `hook/process/process.go`: `parseMounts` returns `["base"]` for an
empty value or one longer than 128 characters and lowercases the
comma-separated names; `readMountConfig` skips paths that do not exist
and rejects a file above 128 entries.
- Default mount lists per product, and the UB devices and tools, checked
against the MindCluster container documentation.
- Built site check: all 27 tutorial pages contain the shared note and
link to `installation.html#installation-ascend-docker-runtime`;
markdownlint and codespell pass on the changed files.
- The basic container start (only `ASCEND_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, no
`--device` or driver `-v` flags) was validated earlier on an A3 host
with runtime 26.1.0 and remains the basis of the first commit.
- The tutorial commands were transformed from the existing
explicit-`--device` blocks with the same device counts; they were not
re-executed on every product. The Quick Start path, which the doctest
workflow covers, gained the runtime requirement and the verification
paragraph; its hardware commands only dropped the device and driver
flags.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: not applicable,
documentation-only change; the limits that the text documents
(128-character mount value, 128 entries per list file, missing host
paths) are covered by the source checks above.
- [ ] **Regression test**: not applicable, no code change.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: not applicable, no code change.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: not applicable, no code change.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: not applicable, no code change.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

---------

Signed-off-by: yangjinyang <yangjinyang5@huawei.com>
Co-authored-by: yjyang62 <yjyang62@users.noreply.github.com>

     **FLA NPU:** Installed explicitly in the common follow-up step for pip, uv, and source installations on A2, A3, and 950DT Products.
 
+#### Use Ascend Docker Runtime {: #installation-ascend-docker-runtime }
+
+Both container-based paths — the prebuilt image and the CANN environment — need Ascend Docker Runtime on the **host**. The runtime mounts the NPU devices and driver paths of the host into the container.
+
+Download the run package from the [MindCluster releases](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/mind-cluster/releases): in `Ascend-docker-runtime_<version>_linux-<arch>.run`, `<version>` is the release you select and `<arch>` is `x86_64` or `aarch64`. Choose a release that supports the Ascend HDK version of the node, then install it as `root` on every node that runs containers:
+
+```bash
+chmod u+x Ascend-docker-runtime_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
+./Ascend-docker-runtime_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --install
+systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart docker
+```
+
+Confirm that the runtime is the default:
+
+{% raw %}
+
+```bash
+docker info --format 'default={{.DefaultRuntime}}'
+```
+
+{% endraw %}
+
+The output must be `default=ascend`. If it prints `runc`, check the `Runtimes:` line of `docker info`:
+
+1. If `ascend` is listed, either add `--runtime ascend` to `docker run`, or set `"default-runtime": "ascend"` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json` and restart Docker.
+2. If `ascend` is missing, rerun the installation and restart Docker.
+
+The container commands in this guide assume Ascend Docker Runtime **26.3.0 or later**, whose default mount lists include `/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info` and `/etc/ascend_install.info`. The installed version is the `version=` field in `/usr/local/Ascend/Ascend-Docker-Runtime/ascend_docker_runtime_install.info` (for example `version=v26.3.0`). With an earlier release, mount those two paths explicitly with `-v <path>:<path>` or upgrade.
+
+To mount an extra host path, create a lowercase `.list` file in `/etc/ascend-docker-runtime.d/`, one path per line, and name it in `ASCEND_RUNTIME_MOUNTS` for the containers that need it, for example `-e ASCEND_RUNTIME_MOUNTS=mylist,base`: that variable replaces the default list, so include `base`; otherwise the container loses the driver libraries and `npu-smi`. The default lists mount `/usr/local/bin/npu-smi`; on a product that installs `npu-smi` under `/usr/local/sbin`, such as Atlas 200I Pro, mount that path explicitly as the tutorial commands do.

@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+These are the `docker run` commands the tutorials used before Ascend Docker Runtime, kept for hosts that cannot install it or choose not to. The runtime reads `ASCEND_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and binds the NPU nodes and driver paths at container start; these commands pass the same nodes with `--device` and the same paths with `-v`, so they also start on a host without the runtime.
+
+For example, [Quick Start](quick_start.md#quick-start-installation) starts its container with one device: `/dev/davinci0`, or `/dev/davinci0` and `/dev/davinci1` on Atlas A3, where an NPU is two DIE devices. The tabs below do the same, and add one `--device /dev/davinciN` line for each further device.
+
+Everything else stays as the tutorial you are adapting writes it: the weight and cache mounts, the ports, the HCCL and network settings, and any extra devices.
+
+=== "Atlas A2 inference products"
+
+    ```bash
+    export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:{{ vllm_ascend_version }}
+    export CONTAINER_NAME=vllm-ascend
+
+    docker run --rm \
+        --name ${CONTAINER_NAME} \
+        --shm-size=1g \
+        --net=host \
+        --device /dev/davinci0 \
+        --device /dev/davinci_manager \
+        --device /dev/devmm_svm \
+        --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
+        -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
+        -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
+        -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
+        -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
+        -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
+        -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
+        -it $IMAGE bash
+    ```
+
+=== "Atlas A3 inference products"
+
+    ```bash
+    export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:{{ vllm_ascend_version }}-a3
+    export CONTAINER_NAME=vllm-ascend
+
+    docker run --rm \
+        --name ${CONTAINER_NAME} \
+        --shm-size=1g \
+        --net=host \
+        --device /dev/davinci0 \
+        --device /dev/davinci1 \
+        --device /dev/davinci_manager \
+        --device /dev/devmm_svm \
+        --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
+        -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
+        -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
+        -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
+        -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
+        -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
+        -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
+        -it $IMAGE bash
+    ```
+
+=== "950DT products"
+
+    The UB device nodes `/dev/ummu` and `/dev/uburma` are not part of the driver library set, so pass them explicitly as well.
+
+    ```bash
+    export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:{{ vllm_ascend_version }}-a5
+    export CONTAINER_NAME=vllm-ascend
+
+    docker run --rm \
+        --name ${CONTAINER_NAME} \
+        --shm-size=1g \
+        --net=host \
+        --device /dev/davinci0 \
+        --device /dev/davinci_manager \
+        --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
+        --device /dev/ummu \
+        --device /dev/uburma \
+        -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
+        -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
+        -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
+        -v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
+        -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
+        -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
+        -it $IMAGE bash
+    ```
+
+=== "Atlas 300I Duo"
+
+    ```bash
+    export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:{{ vllm_ascend_version }}-310p
+    export CONTAINER_NAME=vllm-ascend
+
+    docker run --rm \
+        --name ${CONTAINER_NAME} \
+        --shm-size=1g \
+        --device /dev/davinci0 \
+        --device /dev/davinci_manager \
+        --device /dev/devmm_svm \
+        --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
+        -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
+        -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
+        -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
+        -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
+        -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
+        -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
+        -p 8000:8000 \
+        -it $IMAGE bash
+    ```
+
+=== "Atlas 200I Pro"
+
+    Atlas 200I Pro needs a privileged container plus the device nodes and host files below.
+
+    ```bash
+    export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:{{ vllm_ascend_version }}-310p
+    export MODEL_CACHE="${HOME}/.cache"
+
+    docker run --rm \
+        --privileged \
+        --name vllm-ascend \
+        --shm-size=10g \
+        --device=/dev/davinci0:/dev/davinci0 \
+        --device=/dev/davinci_manager \
+        --device=/dev/ascend_manager \
+        --device=/dev/user_config \
+        -v /etc/sys_version.conf:/etc/sys_version.conf \
+        -v /etc/ld.so.conf.d/mind_so.conf:/etc/ld.so.conf.d/mind_so.conf \
+        -v /etc/hdcBasic.cfg:/etc/hdcBasic.cfg \
+        -v /var/dmp_daemon:/var/dmp_daemon \
+        -v /usr/lib64/libmmpa.so:/usr/lib64/libmmpa.so \
+        -v /usr/lib64/libcrypto.so.1.1:/usr/lib64/libcrypto.so.1.1 \
+        -v /usr/local/sbin/npu-smi:/usr/local/sbin/npu-smi \
+        -v /usr/lib64/libstackcore.so:/usr/lib64/libstackcore.so \
+        -v /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libyaml-0.so.2:/usr/lib64/libyaml-0.so.2 \
+        -v /etc/slog.conf:/etc/slog.conf \
+        -v /var/slogd:/var/slogd \
+        -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64 \
+        -v /usr/lib64/libtensorflow.so:/usr/lib64/libtensorflow.so \
+        -v "$MODEL_CACHE:/root/.cache" \
+        -p 8000:8000 \
+        -it "$IMAGE" bash
+    ```
+
+    On an openEuler host, use the `-310p-openeuler` image, mount `-v /usr/lib64/libsemanage.so.2:/usr/lib64/libsemanage.so.2`, and replace the `libyaml` source with `-v /usr/lib64/libyaml-0.so.2.0.9:/usr/lib64/libyaml-0.so.2`.
+
+Every `--device` line needs its node to exist on the host: `docker run` fails with `no such file or directory` when a device is missing, so drop that line rather than keeping a node the machine does not have. The same applies to the driver and host-file mounts listed above.

[BugFix] Correct Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Mamba state copies on main (#22201)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Mamba state ownership when requests are reordered
or cache blocks are copied, porting the state-copy fix from #21730 to
current `main`.

This PR contains the Mamba state-copy fix (`9ce90eba9`) and the release
note (`f113ad6a6`). It was rebased onto `main` (`099ed02d0`). The
`test_precopy.py` parameter table retains the upstream tile and mapping
combinations and the request-slot regressions.

- Use persistent request slots for pre-copy and postprocess block-table
lookups.
- Avoid duplicate dimension-first convolution copies across tiles.
- Rebuild the Mamba alignment context after KV-cache allocation and
collect ReplaySSM trackers after model-state initialization.
- Retain Mamba state-copy and initialization regressions and document
the persistent-slot indexing and captured-buffer lifetime.

Related work: #20311 also includes overlapping Mamba changes; combining
the branches requires deduplication and validation of the combined
revision.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Correct inaccurate Qwen3.8-Flash-Next outputs on Ascend associated
with reordered request-state mappings and Mamba cache-block copies. No
configuration changes are required.

### How was this patch tested?

- On `f113ad6a6`, Ruff lint and format checks passed for
`test_precopy.py`, and `git diff --check` passed for the PR diff.
- Verified the parameter table retains all five request-slot scenarios,
all three upstream tile and mapping combinations, and both convolution
layouts (12 cases).
- On the earlier Mamba revision `1eae2373`, ran `bash format.sh ci` in
an isolated checkout: 16 hooks passed, including Ruff lint/format,
codespell, typos, Markdown and workflow linting. Two hooks could not
complete locally: gitleaks and its wget fallback are unavailable, and
ShellCheck is not installed. The formatter produced no changes.
- Local pytest/vLLM/Torch/Triton dependencies are unavailable. CPU
integration, NPU and end-to-end validation are delegated to CI on this
exact PR head. Earlier hardware results in the discussion apply to their
recorded revisions.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] Retained request-slot state ownership and initialization
regression coverage.
- [x] Verified the PR contains the Mamba fix and its release note.
- [x] Completed the available local static checks.
- [ ] Latest-head CPU/NPU CI and hardware performance validation.

[Feature][KV Pool] Enable prefill KV offload for GLM-5.3 (#22742)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable GLM-5.3 prefill KV offload with BF16 and FP8 C8. For single-group
offload, reshape the shared slot to match the component layout with
offload disabled so P/D can use the same transfer layout.

```text
FP8 C8 Indexer
  Offload disabled  [K0][K1] [scale0][scale1]  (native buffer)
  Offload enabled   [K0][K1] [scale0][scale1]  (shared slot)

BF16 main MLA
  Offload disabled  [NoPE0][NoPE1]              (NoPE tensor)
                    [RoPE0][RoPE1]              (RoPE tensor)
  Offload enabled   [NoPE0][NoPE1] [RoPE0][RoPE1]  (shared slot)
```

Mooncake Push with offload depends on #21891.

#### P/D startup

Use the V2 runner on separate P and D hosts with matching KV cache
formats and a shared MemCache service. The P example uses four shared
buffers per block-stride bucket.

**P node**

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" --kv-transfer-config '{
  "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_producer",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "connectors": [
      {"kv_connector": "MooncakePushConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer"},
      {
        "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector",
        "kv_role": "kv_producer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config": {
          "backend": "memcache",
          "use_layerwise": true,
          "layerwise_num_shared_buffers": 4,
          "layerwise_independent_layers": []
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}'
```

**D node**

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" --kv-transfer-config '{
  "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "connectors": [
      {"kv_connector": "MooncakePushConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"},
      {
        "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector",
        "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config": {
          "backend": "memcache",
          "use_layerwise": false
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}'
```

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No

### How was this patch tested?

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

---------

Signed-off-by: gq-bao <gavin.gq.bao@gmail.com>

[Feature] QLI v2: candidate-driven execution, QSLI metadata operator, and arch22 performance optimizations (#21394)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds candidate-driven execution to the Quant Lightning Indexer
(QLI) v2
kernel on arch22, introduces a standalone QSLI (quant sparse lightning
indexer)
metadata operator, and lands a series of verified performance
optimizations and
correctness fixes for Ascend 910B-class hardware.

**Why:** QLI v2 scoring is dominated by scanning the full KV sequence,
while in
decode and long-context workloads most blocks cannot reach the top-K
anyway. The
candidate-driven design lets the producer emit a compact candidate block
list and
its length, so the consumer can restrict its work to those candidates
instead of
scanning everything. Previously this path existed in the kernel but was
not
reachable from production: the mode=2 entry ignored
`candidate_block_length`, and
the source path (mode=1) did not produce it.

**What it does:**

1. **Kernel optimizations (arch22)** — adaptive Top-K accumulator width
and
Level-0 vector-repeat dispatch (from #20303); query/weight resident in
L0A;
   block-level hit-bitmap candidate mask; fully vectorized block-level
   mask/kscale/index generation; candidate tile 256→512 tokens;
ping-pong score/kscale prefetch; threshold pruning with row-level early
exit;
   hardware compare + `Select` mask chain.
2. **Candidate-driven pipeline** — `candidate_mode=2` with
`candidate_block_length`: staging gather / cube QK / vector scoring
TopK,
8-slot semaphore ring, W double buffering, score double buffering, and a
   pending queue for deferred cross-task consumption.
3. **QSLI metadata operator** — new AICPU operator
`VllmAscendQuantSparseLightningIndexerMetadata` that schedules work by
`max(L)×8` tokens with candidate tiles, plus QSLI candidate × FD/LD
fusion.
4. **Cross-core reduction (LD) on 910B** — LD was previously
Ascend950-only; it
is now enabled on 910B, and block-level topk spill/reduce was added so
mode=1
   block outputs also work under LD.
5. **Closed source→consumer loop** — mode=1 now optionally emits
`candidate_block_length` (DSL semantics: candidate blocks of 8 tokens),
and
the adapter consumer passes it through and builds QSLI metadata on
demand.
6. **Correctness fixes** found during validation: LD slot addressing and
`DataCopyExtParams.srcStride` units; NaN poisoning from stale invalid
slots;
   FD last-tile non-integral-block precision (L=321 class); score-region
ping-pong overwritten by a third task on the same core; aux(kscale)
region
parity overwrite (period 2→4); and a cube K-load handshake lost during
the
   upstream merge.

This is a large PR (22 commits, 46 files). Each commit message contains
the
detailed design notes, measurements, and validation evidence for that
step;
reviewing commit by commit is recommended.

**Measured results** (msprof device-side Task Duration on Ascend 910B3
unless
noted; same-environment paired controls):

| Change | Workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q/W resident in L0A | cases A / B | −6.9% / −5.7% |
| Block-level hit bitmap | case C candidate consumer | −16.9% |
| Vectorized candidate consumption | case C, L=2048 | 2491.8 → 675.4 µs
(−72.9%) |
| Candidate tile 256→512 | case C, L=2048 | 690.9 → 544.5 µs (−21.2%) |
| Threshold pruning | case C | 525.9 → 485.0 µs (−7.8%) |
| Row-level early exit | case C | 479.8 → ~323 µs (~−33%) |
| QSLI candidate × FD fusion | decode B16/S1=1/S2=128K | 137.4 → 125.1
µs (−9.0%) |
| Block-level LD for mode=1 | cand1_src | 0.181 → 0.145 ms (−19.9%) |

The row-level early-exit number was measured with torch aclprof
(calibrated
against msprof Task Duration within 0.06%) and was still pending an
msprof
re-check.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, but additively only:

- `npu_quant_lightning_indexer_v3` gains an optional input
`candidate_block_length` and an optional output
`candidate_block_length_out`
  (`int32`, `[rows, N2]`, allocated only in source mode).
- New AICPU operator `VllmAscendQuantSparseLightningIndexerMetadata` for
QSLI
  metadata.
- Existing call sites and modes keep their current behavior (the old
2-output
entry receives an empty placeholder); outputs are row-by-row identical
to the
  previous implementation on all regression cases.
- The adapter-internal `_qli_newapi_block_length` helper is removed
because the
  kernel now produces the length; no other public Python API changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Vendor e2e regression:** 17 cases (mode=1 / mode=3 /
candidate-source / FD /
  mask0 / topk2048 / prefill / g64), row-by-row identical to pre-change
  baselines (dump A/B), including block-level outputs.
- **Generalization sweep:** 33/33 cases — unaligned L, multi-batch,
varlen,
  decode, mask0, cmp2, mixed L, out-of-order page tables.
- **Boundary coverage:** `L ∈ {1, 63, 64, 65, 321, 2047, 2048}`; L=321
×10;
`L ∈ {321, 325, 352, 383, 384, 385, 449, 511, 512, 2048}`; empty rows
and
  `V ≤ 0` rows; core counts 1–32.
- **Goldens:** case C independent golden 49152/49152; source→consumer
closed
  loop 512/512 × 12 rows; `verify_qsli_meta` A/B/C/D 7/7; numpy golden.
- **Probes:** prefix alternation, W sign flip, stale data, hot window,
metadata
  ABI, `QLI_CHECK_QSLI_META=1` self-check.
- **New e2e test:** `test_quant_lightning_indexer_vector_repeats.py` for
the
  Level-0 vector-repeat dispatch.
- **Performance:** msprof device-side Task Duration (30/23/26-run
protocols as
noted per commit), with same-session interleaved A/B controls for small
deltas.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

+
+`VllmAscendQuantSparseLightningIndexerMetadata` 是 QLI v2 主算子 **candidate 模式（mode=2）**
+配套的独立 AICPU 调度算子。它在设备侧计算每个 AI Core 应处理的
+`(batch, gS1 块, 候选 tile)` 区间，供主算子的候选驱动路径使用。
+
+## 与 QLI metadata 的关系（重要）
+
+- **两份 metadata 分开实现、不可混用**：QSLI metadata 的输出是 QSLI 私有语义的
+  `int32[1024]`（前 36 条 LI、第 36 条起 LD 记录，布局与 QLI 相同但**字段语义不同**）；
+- 本算子的工作量按 `max(L) × 8` token、**候选 tile = 256 token** 计算；
+  QLI metadata 按可见 S2 长度、S2 tile（910B 为 2048 token）计算；
+- 主算子在接收到 `candidate_block_length` 时必须搭配本算子生成的 metadata，
+  不能使用 QLI metadata 替代。
+
+## 输入 / 输出
+
+| 参数 | 类型 | 说明 |
+|---|---|---|
+| `candidate_block_length` | INT32 `[T,1]` 或 `[T]`，**必选** | 每行有效候选块数（DSL 语义，一候选块 = 8 token） |
+| `cu_seqlens_q/k`、`seqused_q/k`、`cmp_residual_k` | INT32，可选 | 序列长度信息，语义同 QLI |
+| 属性 | | `num_heads_q/k`、`head_dim`、`topk`、`quant_mode`、`layout_q/k`、`mask_mode`、`cmp_ratio` 等 |
+| `metadata` | INT32 `[1024]` | 输出，QSLI 私有调度信息 |
+
+## V1 范围
+
+- **不做 FD/S2 分片**（`supportFd_ = false`）：按整行（gS1 块）调度、主算子直出；
+  原因是主算子"候选 × FD 归并"路径尚未通过正确性验证（候选分片归并 bug）。
+- 工作量按 `max(L)×8`，分核粒度是一个 gS1 块（mBaseSize = 4 行）。
+
+## 已知问题（2026-11-03）
+
+主算子的候选驱动路径在 **1~2 token 的 gS1 块**（M=32/64）上分数不正确
+（4-token 块正常）。本算子本身只负责调度，不受影响；但端到端使用前需先修复主算子
+（见 `scripts/prof_output/qli_v2_caseopt/RESULT_candidate_driven.md` §9）。
+
+## 构建
+
+```bash
+cd csrc
+source <CANN>/set_env.sh
+bash build.sh --pkg --soc=ascend910b --vendor_name=<name> \
+  --ops=quant_lightning_indexer_v2,quant_lightning_indexer_v2_metadata,quant_sparse_lightning_indexer_metadata -j32
+```

[Doc] Fix Hy4 Preview host networking and JSON formatting (#22995)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Hy4 Preview multi-node instructions require host networking, but the
container creation example omitted it. Add `--net=host` to the Docker
command and explicitly state the requirement for both nodes in Section
5.2 so the documented host IPs can be used for DP/HCCL communication.

Also make comma spacing consistent in the three speculative decoding
JSON command examples.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No runtime/API changes; this is a small documentation correction. No
release note fragment is needed.

### How was this patch tested?

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Parsed all four speculative decoding JSON snippets and checked their
expected values: passed.
- Ran `bash -n` on all nine Bash code blocks: passed.
- `bash format.sh ci`: all checks passed except shellcheck, which could
not run because the local shellcheck binary is not installed. Markdown
lint passed.
- Commit hooks for the changed Markdown file: passed.
- Documentation build was not run (mkdocs is not installed). No runtime
tests were added for this documentation-only change. Multi-node NPU
validation was not run locally; hardware validation remains for
CI/reviewers.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [x] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [x] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

- Align the A3 W8A8 Prefill startup parameters in ordinary PD and KV
Pool deployments, including CANN MegaMoE with `enable_fused_mc2=2`.
- Document the `cann_ops_transformer` dependency and the shared
scheduler and graph overrides for 4K inputs.

section anchors resolve in the generated page.

inference arguments, and validated the expanded connector JSON and
topology. The default and 4K A3 Prefill arguments were also checked with
a mock `vllm` command.

installation did not finish within the bounded local attempt.

repeated-prefix pool hits, SSD offload, memory use, and performance
still require real hardware evidence.

[Feature][A3] Support W4A8 MegaMoe shared-expert fusion (#22128)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Builds on #22207 to enable MegaMoE shared-expert fusion on A3 for
DeepSeek V4.1 with W4A8 (INT4) routed experts and a dynamic W8A8 (INT8)
shared expert.

- Passes shared weights and scales through both W4A8 weight storage
paths to MegaMoE, reusing the shared INT8 descriptors from #22207.
- Loads full shared weights on each TP rank when shared-expert DP is
enabled for the A3 main model.
- Checks for a CANN interface with independent routed and shared weight
descriptors. The runner skips the separate shared MLP only when the
shared weights are ready and the current forward uses MegaMoE.
- Sizes the A3 mode-3 symmetric buffer for the profiling token budget on
decode-only nodes, including the 432-request, 512-profile-token case.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

Yes. On A3, a supported W4A8 model can now fuse its dynamic W8A8 shared
expert with the routed experts. With a matching CANN operator package,
keep `--enable-expert-parallel` and add the following fields to the
existing `--additional-config` JSON.

```json
{"enable_fused_mc2": 3, "enable_shared_expert_dp": true}
```

### How was this patch tested?

- Ruff lint, Ruff format, Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check`
passed on the updated source.
- Statically checked that the A3 CANN 9.3 B106 Python wheel exposes the
shared weights, scales and dtype arguments required by the mixed
INT4/INT8 path. Also verified PD service startup and real-model
inference on the r140 A3 image with the matching prebuilt B106 operator
package. The r140 measurements are reported below.
- Updated regression coverage for ABI detection, W4A8 payload
forwarding, shared weight replication, runner fallback and decode-only
profiling capacity.

**A3 r140 validation (2026-11-23 to 2026-11-24)**

Tested revision `df8eceedaac2e9836043863236e73b8bc8ca10aa` on two Ascend
A3 nodes using the ARM64 main r140 image (CANN 9.3.0), the matching B106
MegaMoE operator package, and `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8` weights.
The image pinned vLLM at `4ba787ec` and vLLM-Ascend at `c12397a0`. The
performance baseline is r140 + #22207. The candidate adds #22128. Both
use the same weights, package, service flags and workload, with no
additional code patches.

**Pure decode performance**

Both variants use P DP4/TP1/PCP4, D DP16/TP1/PCP1, `enable_fused_mc2=3`
on P and D, P-side EPLB, MooncakeConnectorV2, fixed DSpark5, V2 Model
Runner, FASTOKENS and four proxy workers. D uses
`max_num_batched_tokens=432`, `max_num_seqs=72` and
`gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`. Startup evidence confirms that the
baseline executes the shared expert separately for A3 W4A8 and the
candidate takes the fused path.

Each case used the same 128K input and 1,024-token output, one fully
warmed P-side prefix, and request rate 0 (unpaced). Throughput is
steady-state D-side generated tokens/s. The baseline averages two
repetitions. For each candidate case, the highest and lowest throughput
of six repetitions were dropped, and latency metrics use the same four
retained runs.

| Concurrency / requests | Steady D throughput, tok/s | Mean TTFT, s |
Mean TPOT, ms | Mean ITL, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 306 / 1,224 | 9,910.08 → 11,230.84 (**+13.33%**) | 1.741 → 1.605
(−7.82%) | 28.90 → 25.03 (−13.41%) | 109.45 → 95.33 (−12.91%) |
| 432 / 1,728 | 11,123.47 → 11,441.82 (+2.86%) | 6.714 → 8.844 (+31.72%)
| 31.60 → 28.15 (−10.92%) | 119.25 → 106.18 (−10.96%) |

At 306 concurrency, the candidate is also 5.37% above the faster
baseline run. At 432 concurrency, the throughput difference is within
observed run-to-run variation. Decode capacity queueing increased, and
TTFT rose even as TPOT and ITL improved. Neither variant recorded D-side
preemptions or recompute warnings during these runs.

**Accuracy with #22128**

The scores below are from candidate runs. No matching r140 run without
#22128 was evaluated for either dataset, so these scores cannot
establish an accuracy delta attributable to the PR.

| Benchmark | Result |
|---|---|
| GPQA Diamond (AISBench, dataset revision `b1ed2c`) | **178 / 198
correct (89.90%)**, with **100%** answer extraction. Native AISBench
score. |
| DeepSWE | **85 passed, 27 failed, 1 unjudged** out of 113 tasks.
**75.22%** confirmed passes over all tasks, **75.89%** over the 112
judged tasks. A verifier timeout on both the original attempt and the
single retry left the full-suite score incomplete. |

GPQA used an earlier r140 serving configuration with P/D
`enable_fused_mc2=2/3`, MooncakeHybridConnector and D
`max_num_batched_tokens=512`. Sampling used `temperature=1.0`,
`top_p=1.0`, a 131,072-token output limit, concurrency 64, and
`chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": true, "reasoning_effort": 100}`.

DeepSWE used the selected r140 candidate configuration from the
performance table. It ran on four evaluator workers with verified
per-session prefill affinity. Sampling used `temperature=1.0`,
`top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=393216`, and
`chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": true, "reasoning_effort": "max"}`.
The readiness pilot is excluded from the scores.

---

**Historical GPQA Diamond (r91 / CANN 9.2.1)**

The MegaMoE + shared-expert run completed **198/198 requests**. The
score below is the original AISBench score, without answer-format
normalization:

| Validation run | Correct / total | Native accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|
| MegaMoE + shared-expert validation | 176 / 198 | **88.89%** |

The fusion run used `temperature=1`, `top_p=1`, thinking enabled,
`reasoning_effort=100`, maximum output 131,072 and concurrency 64; no
response hit the output limit. Six answers used forms such as `ANSWER:
$A` that the native extractor did not recognize. A supplementary
format-only review scored 182/198 (91.92%); the table retains the
original 88.89% score.

[Doc] Refresh GLM PD configurations and tutorial guidance (#22699)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Refresh GLM-5.3-Flash A3 ordinary PD from the supplied configuration:
Prefill DP1/TP1/PCP16 and Decode DP16/TP1, MTP5 and ReplaySSM, updated
EPLB and Decode fine-grained TP/graph settings. Align launch commands,
health checks, proxy endpoints and parameter descriptions. Explicit
pooling overrides preserve its existing DP2/TP1/PCP8 Prefill and DP8/TP2
Decode configuration.

Includes the GLM-5.3 A3 ordinary-PD speculative configuration correction
and documentation review fixes from #22281. Recent merged GLM-5.3 A3 and
Flash 950DT PD updates are already in both target branches. Align Flash
950DT pooling non-pooling parameters with ordinary PD, adding only the
pool connectors and Memcache environment while retaining ordinary PD
ReplaySSM and other serving parameters. Set Flash A3 ordinary-PD Decode
HCCL_BUFFSIZE to 1200; A3 pooling remains at 1024.

Update the GLM-5.3 950DT ordinary-PD Decode example to the supplied
DFlash7 configuration: HCCL buffer 300, batch budget 80, HND cache
layout, disabled Decode prefix caching, output-projection TP8 and
MooncakeConnectorV2 plus 4 GiB/rank PreemptOffloadConnector. Keep
Prefill scripts unchanged and use a configurable local DFlash2
checkpoint path. Profiling settings remain excluded. Update topology
prose, KV ports and the recommendation table.

Align all three GLM-5.3 A3 scenarios with the supplied scripts. Ordinary
PD already matches; pooling now uses the same 135k TP1/PCP16/PP2 Prefill
and DP16/TP2 Decode with a standalone MemCache pool and role-specific
layerwise settings. The 1M example uses TP16/PP2/DCP16 Prefill and
DP4/TP8/DCP8 Decode. Update 41/37 PP partition, launch ranks, proxy
endpoints, scheduling limits, glm5 request names and recommendations.
All 12 role scripts were checked against the supplied runtime options,
including shell syntax, expanded arguments and JSON.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Documentation examples only. Only three GLM Markdown files change; no PO
files or runtime code changes.

### How was this patch tested?
- English and Chinese strict MkDocs builds passed on main and
releases/v0.33.0rc.
- Markdown lint and git diff --check passed.
- A3 ordinary-PD shell syntax, expanded arguments, JSON, DP1 rank
filtering and all 17 proxy endpoints checked locally.
- English/Chinese rendered anchors, topology and version macro expansion
checked.
- The three GLM documents are identical between the two PR branches.
- Full format.sh ci was attempted but stalled installing the actionlint
environment; full-hook validation is left to CI.
- CI testing only for hardware behavior; no NPU runtime or performance
test was performed.

[BugFix] Bind visible NPUs to the --device-ids selection (#22495)

Verified on Ascend 910B (vLLM 0.33.0, CANN 9.3.0): visible=2,3 with
--device-ids 1 leaves chip 2 with no process at all while chip 3 serves
requests normally.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

With ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5 and --device-ids 1, vLLM resolves the
model architecture before any worker binds its NPU. That import path
reaches flash_linear_attention's get_all_max_shared_mem(), which queries
every device in device_count(); torch_npu creates an ACL context per
query, so chip 4 is initialized as well and npu-smi reports the service
on both cards.
Narrow ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the chips selected by --device-ids
and renumber the ids to 0..N-1 at EngineArgs.create_engine_config,
before create_model_config() imports the model.
assigned_physical_gpu_ids keeps the full selection, so the worker-side
two-stage device mapping is unchanged and child processes inherit the
narrowed set. No-op for absent/UUID ids, Ray, or an
out-of-range/unchanged selection.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
no
### How was this patch tested?
Verify on A3: visible=2,3. When using --device-ids 1, there are no
processes on chip 2, while chip 3 can process requests normally.

I

(exceptions,

and are

- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

+## Device probing in the engine core
+
+vLLM resolves the model architecture while it builds the engine configuration,
+before any worker binds an NPU. That import path probes every *visible* device,
+and the NPU runtime creates a context for each probed chip. A launch that reaches
+vLLM through its command line is normalized by vLLM Ascend: the visible set is
+narrowed to the chips named by `--device-ids` before the model is imported, so no
+other chip is initialized.
+
+The Python API has no equivalent hook. When you construct `LLM(...)` or
+`EngineArgs(...)` yourself, express the selection through the visible set instead
+of a wider set plus `device_ids`. Set the variable before importing `vllm` or
+`torch_npu`; `device_ids` can then be omitted, or set to the contiguous indices
+`0..N-1`:

+import os
+
+os.environ["ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = "5"
+
+from vllm import LLM
+
+llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B")

[Misc][Refactor] Remove leftover DeepSeek V4 legacy KV cache allocation code (#22997)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow-up cleanup for #21083 (RFC #21053).

In #21083, DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 KV cache allocation was migrated to
`unified_allocate_kv_cache` in `allocate_kv_cache_main` and the legacy
DSV4/V4.1 reshape branches in `_reshape_kv_cache_v2` were removed.
However, the legacy `_is_dsv4_model` helper and the `if is_dsv4_model:`
shared-backing branch in `_allocate_kv_cache` were left behind as
unreachable dead code.

This PR removes that leftover legacy allocation code and updates the
corresponding unit tests:

- Remove `_is_dsv4_model` and the unreachable `if is_dsv4_model:`
allocation branch in `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/attn_utils.py`.
- Migrate DSV4 KV cache allocation unit tests in
`tests/ut/worker/test_attn_utils_v2.py` and
`tests/ut/worker/test_turboquant_v2.py` from legacy `_allocate_kv_cache`
to `allocate_kv_cache_main` / `unified_allocate_kv_cache`.
- Remove obsolete `_is_dsv4_model` monkeypatches across worker/offload
unit tests.

No. This is an internal dead-code cleanup with no user-facing behavior
change.

[Performance][Model] Reuse DeepSeek V4.1 routing input IDs across DP/PCP (#19679)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 hash and vision routers need token IDs in the same row
order as the router logits. On the `ALLGATHER` path, successive MoE
layers repeat the same collective within a decoder segment.

The first eligible layer gathers the IDs after its MoE prepare step has
established the SP/DP/PCP row layout. It copies the result into
model-owned storage at a fixed address. Later layers read the active
rows. The cache preserves the input dtype (INT32 or INT64) and the raw
`-1` sentinel. The fused Hash TopK operator handles the sentinel on
load. The PyTorch vision path normalizes its own input before indexing.

The decoder prefix and bounded-replay tail each have a producer and
separate storage because replay can compact rows. Each producer
refreshes its buffer on every execution of its segment. Model
initialization uses the communication policy at the largest supported
padded batch to skip allocation where `ALLGATHER` is unreachable. Other
communication paths and concurrent microbatches prepare IDs per layer.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal performance optimization with no new CLI
arguments or environment variables.

### How was this patch tested?

#### 1. Regression Tests

- The routing-ID, compile, distributed, fused MoE and Engram shared-pool
CPU tests passed (241 tests). This includes a compiled forward through
the opaque MoE op and four real Gloo ranks with DP2 × PCP2.
- `bash format.sh ci` passed on the PR diff against main.
- The single-card A2 graph replay test passed on `9a57858f1`. It checks
that a captured consumer sees the IDs written by eager and captured
producers when alternating between graph sizes. The collective is
simulated. [A2 CI
log](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45350506268/job/138301079643)

#### 2. Serving Benchmark (Ascend A2)

These measurements use the November 15 baseline and predate the upstream
Hash TopK input change in #21452. The merged revision has yet to be
benchmarked.
- **Setup:** `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` (W4A8), A2 TP8 (DP1/PCP1, EP
enabled), `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`,
`--max-model-len 262144`, MTP disabled (100 requests, 5.0M input / 35K
output tokens).
- **Highlights:** Output throughput improved by **+1.52% ~ +1.71%**, and
mean TPOT decreased by **1.47% ~ 2.16%**.

| Concurrency | Metric | Baseline | IDs Reuse | Diff |
| :---: | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **6** | Output Throughput (tok/s) | 152.43 | 154.74 | **+1.52%** |
| | TPOT mean / P99 (ms) | 32.01 / 35.49 | 31.54 / 34.95 | **-1.47%** |
| | Mean ITL (ms) | 32.99 | 32.38 | **-1.85%** |
| | Mean TTFT / E2EL (ms) | 2354.06 / 13524.71 | 2313.59 / 13322.17 |
-1.72% / -1.50% |
| **15** | Output Throughput (tok/s) | 268.27 | 272.86 | **+1.71%** |
| | Mean TPOT (ms) | 40.32 / 49.38 | 39.45 / 48.54 |  **-2.16%**  |
| | Mean ITL (ms) | 41.75 | 40.57 | **-2.83%** |
| | Mean TTFT / E2EL (ms) | 4703.21 / 18776.56 | 4695.92 / 18464.51 |
-0.16% / -1.66% |

#### 3. Accuracy Evaluation
- **GSM8K:** `0.9757` on the previously evaluated revision.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

Signed-off-by: Yao Liu <liuyao0929@gmail.com>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Single-NPU graph dataflow coverage; the collective is simulated, not HCCL."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import torch
+import torch_npu  # noqa: F401
+
+from vllm_ascend.ascend_forward_context import MoECommType
+from vllm_ascend.ops.fused_moe.router import fused_topk_router as router_module
+
+
+def test_routing_ids_refresh_across_separate_graphs(monkeypatch):
+    bucket_sizes = (3, 7)
+    remote_ids = {size: torch.arange(size, dtype=torch.int32, device="npu") + 100 for size in bucket_sizes}
+    gather = MagicMock(side_effect=lambda ids: torch.cat((ids, remote_ids[ids.numel()])))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        router_module,
+        "_EXTRA_CTX",
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            moe_comm_type=MoECommType.ALLGATHER,
+            moe_comm_method=SimpleNamespace(prepare_finalize=SimpleNamespace(all_gather_input_ids=gather)),
+        ),
+    )
+    producer = router_module.AscendFusedTopKRouter(top_k=2, global_num_experts=4)
+    consumer = router_module.AscendFusedTopKRouter(top_k=2, global_num_experts=4)
+    buffer = torch.empty(2 * max(bucket_sizes), dtype=torch.int64, device="npu")
+    producer.routing_input_ids_buffer = buffer
+    producer.is_routing_input_ids_producer = True
+    consumer.routing_input_ids_buffer = buffer
+
+    captures = []
+    for size in bucket_sizes:
+        input_ids = torch.arange(size, dtype=torch.int32, device="npu")
+        num_rows = 2 * size
+        for _ in range(3):
+            producer._prepare_routing_input_ids(input_ids, num_rows)
+            calls_after_producer = gather.call_count
+            consumer._prepare_routing_input_ids(input_ids, num_rows).clone()
+            assert gather.call_count == calls_after_producer
+        torch.npu.synchronize()
+
+        producer_graph = torch.npu.NPUGraph()
+        calls_before_capture = gather.call_count
+        with torch.npu.graph(producer_graph):
+            producer._prepare_routing_input_ids(input_ids, num_rows)
+        assert gather.call_count == calls_before_capture + 1
+
+        consumer_graph = torch.npu.NPUGraph()
+        with torch.npu.graph(consumer_graph):
+            # A device-side consumer is required: returning only a view would
+            # not exercise the address recorded by the consumer graph.
+            output = consumer._prepare_routing_input_ids(input_ids, num_rows).clone()
+        assert gather.call_count == calls_before_capture + 1
+        captures.append((input_ids, producer_graph, consumer_graph, output))
+
+    # Alternate graph buckets after both are captured. Also write the shared
+    # buffer from an eager producer while retaining the captured consumer.
+    for step, (bucket, eager_producer) in enumerate(((0, False), (1, False), (0, True), (1, True), (0, False))):
+        input_ids, producer_graph, consumer_graph, output = captures[bucket]
+        size = input_ids.numel()
+        local_cpu = torch.arange(size, dtype=torch.int32) + 1000 * (step + 1)
+        remote_cpu = torch.arange(size, dtype=torch.int32) + 2000 * (step + 1)
+        local_cpu[0] = -1
+        local_cpu[1] = 0
+        remote_cpu[-1] = -1
+        input_ids.copy_(local_cpu)
+        remote_ids[size].copy_(remote_cpu)
+        buffer.fill_(-999)
+        calls_before_replay = gather.call_count
+        if eager_producer:
+            producer._prepare_routing_input_ids(input_ids, 2 * size)
+        else:
+            producer_graph.replay()
+        consumer_graph.replay()
+        torch.npu.synchronize()
+
+        expected = torch.cat((local_cpu, remote_cpu))
+        torch.testing.assert_close(output.cpu(), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        # Python callbacks execute during eager/capture, never graph replay.
+        # Each eager producer calls gather once; consumers never call it.
+        assert gather.call_count == calls_before_replay + int(eager_producer)

[Performance][KV Transfer] Support per-request Mooncake V2 pulls (#20903)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Mooncake V2 currently waits for every READ in a producer-engine batch
before reporting request completion. A request whose KV is ready can
therefore wait for unrelated transfers before decode becomes runnable.

This PR defaults to submitting and completing requests independently.
Each request retains its batch index for replica selection and reuses
block mappings across layers and PP ranks. Future callbacks report
completion only after all submitted READs for that request finish,
including after a partial submission failure. Later requests can
complete independently.

The receive loop selects its batch or per-request queue processor once
at initialization. Each processor owns queue completion and exception
handling. Callback-registration failures drain submitted READs through
an idempotent completion path; unexpected batch-aggregation failures
drain known READs before reporting failure. Unexpected bookkeeping
failures are logged so other producer engines can continue; requests
whose completion cannot be established are retained rather than
releasing potentially in-flight blocks.

Both modes prepare addresses and execute synchronous READs in the
transfer pool. Batch mode retains aggregated READs and its completion
barrier. Thread-pool configuration is shared in the base worker and also
applies to Push sending workers. Block-hash handling and NumPy address
optimizations are outside this PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Configure these options in `kv_connector_extra_config`:

| Option | Default | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pull_transfer_mode` | `"request"` | Pull only, on D: independent
request submission/completion. Use `"batch"` for aggregated READs and
batch completion. |
| `transfer_max_workers` | `32` | Positive integer controlling the
transfer pool per worker: D-side READs for Pull, P-side sends for Push.
Booleans and strings are rejected. |

```json
{"kv_connector_extra_config": {"pull_transfer_mode": "request", "transfer_max_workers": 32}}
```

For Push, set only `transfer_max_workers` on P. The peer requires no
matching setting. This replaces the earlier draft's `pull_max_workers`
option. Request mode can increase READ call overhead; its end-to-end
performance benefit has not been established.

### How was this patch tested?

- Focused tests cover shared pool configuration, Push pool wiring, READ
granularity and byte-range equivalence, independent completion after
submission/READ failures, callback registration failures before/after
attachment, immediate/repeated callbacks, and continued processing of
another producer engine after an unexpected handler or batch-aggregation
failure.
- **26 local CPU source-isolated cases passed** using actual production
methods and test functions, synthetic metadata, real Futures/threads and
mocked device/transport initialization. These are not full torch/vLLM
runtime pytest results.
- `format.sh ci` passed for enabled hooks, including Ruff, codespell,
typos and Markdown lint. Long-function and symbolic-meta checks were run
with native Python, and the logger check with Git Bash. `git diff
--check` passed.
- Full runtime tests, native Mooncake transport, NPU
accuracy/performance and CI remain unverified. No NPU services were
started. Windows limitations remain for actionlint bootstrap,
unavailable shellcheck and the gitleaks hook's `/bin/bash` dependency;
these were skipped, not reported as passing.

Run the affected tests in a compatible runtime:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_base_worker.py tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_pull_worker.py tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_push_worker.py
```

AI assistance was used for implementation and local validation.

### Checklist

- [x] Request completion and failure-draining regression coverage
- [x] Shared configuration and byte-range equivalence checks
- [ ] Full runtime tests and CI passed
- [ ] NPU accuracy and controlled performance comparison completed

+### Mooncake V2 Transfer Configuration
+
+Set these options in `kv_connector_extra_config`. Pull uses the decoder's
+transfer pool; Push uses the prefiller's sending pool.
+
+| Option | Default | Behavior |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `pull_transfer_mode` | `"request"` | Pull only: submit and complete each request independently. Use `"batch"` to aggregate READs and wait for the whole producer-engine batch. |
+| `transfer_max_workers` | `32` | Positive integer controlling the transfer pool size per worker: D-side READs for Pull, P-side sends for Push. Booleans and strings are rejected. |
+
+```json
+{"kv_connector_extra_config": {"pull_transfer_mode": "request", "transfer_max_workers": 32}}
+```
+
+For Push, set only `transfer_max_workers` on the producer. The peer requires no
+matching setting. Both Pull modes prepare addresses and
+execute READs in the transfer pool, and wait for submitted READs to finish before
+reporting a failed receive. Request mode avoids the batch completion barrier but
+can increase READ call overhead; compare both modes under the same workload.
+
 ### QoS Configuration
 
 Set `qos_priority` in the transfer initiator's `kv_connector_extra_config`.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("registration", ["before", "after", "completed"])
+def test_callback_registration_failure_drains_and_finishes_once(registration, monkeypatch):
+    thread = make_thread()
+    futures: list[Future[None]] = [Future() for _ in range(3)]
+    futures[0].set_result(None)
+    entered = threading.Event()
+    original = futures[1].add_done_callback
+    callbacks = []
+
+    def register(callback):
+        callbacks.append(callback)
+        if registration != "before":
+            original(callback)
+        if registration == "completed":
+            futures[1].set_result(None)
+        entered.set()
+        raise RuntimeError("callback registration failed")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(futures[1], "add_done_callback", register)
+    tasks = {future: (0, 0, rank, {"a"}) for rank, future in enumerate(futures)}
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as executor:
+        tracking = executor.submit(thread._track_request, "a", make_req_meta(local=([10],)), tasks, None)
+        try:
+            assert entered.wait(5)
+            assert thread.finished_requests.empty()
+            assert not thread.invalid_block_ids
+            if not futures[1].done():
+                futures[1].set_result(None)
+            assert thread.finished_requests.empty()  # The third READ still owns blocks.
+            futures[2].set_result(None)
+            tracking.result(timeout=5)
+            assert thread.finished_requests.get_nowait() == ("a", True)
+            callbacks[0](futures[1])  # A late/repeated callback must not publish twice.
+            assert thread.finished_requests.empty()
+            assert thread.invalid_block_ids == {10}
+        finally:
+            for future in futures:
+                if not future.done():
+                    future.set_result(None)
+

[BugFix][Quantization] Pad odd W4A8-MXFP4 MoE down_proj scale groups under TP (#21399)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`AscendW4A8MXFPDynamicFusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading`
reshapes `w2_weight_scale`'s
last dimension into pairs of MX groups. A TP shard can leave
`intermediate_size_per_partition // group_size` odd (e.g.
`moe_intermediate_size=2304`,
`group_size=32`, `tensor_parallel_size=8` gives `288 // 32 = 9`), which
crashes the reshape
with a shape mismatch.

This is the same class of bug as #20398 / #20573 (DS-original W8A8 MXFP8
linear path hitting
an odd scale-group count under TP), just in the FP4 MoE routed-expert
path. Pads with one
zero group before reshaping, mirroring that fix and vLLM upstream's own
MXFP4 scale-alignment
pad (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/mxfp4_utils.py`).

**Caveat (updated):** unlike the W8A8 MXFP8 fix, this only pads
`w2_weight_scale`, not
`w2_weight` itself. I looked for a kernel-side shape check that could
make this unsafe, the
way I was burned on a since-closed sibling PR (#21398) where a kernel
turned out to hardcode a
contract I'd assumed was a bug. The actual GEMM2 kernel this scale feeds
into is closed-source
(`torch_npu`/CANN binary, no Python wrapper to inspect), so I can't rule
that out by reading
source the way I could there.

What I *can* show: for this model specifically, this PR's precondition
(odd scale-group count)
and #21397's precondition (`intermediate_size_per_partition` not a
multiple of 64, i.e. SwiGLU
activation width not 128-aligned) are mathematically the same condition
in disguise —
`intermediate_size_per_partition % 64 == 0` implies
`(intermediate_size_per_partition / 32)` is
even, and conversely an odd scale-group count implies
`intermediate_size_per_partition % 64 != 0`.
So on `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` there is no tensor-parallel size at which
this PR's code path runs
without also hitting #21397 first (SwiGLU quant happens before the
down_proj GEMM this scale
feeds). That means I categorically cannot exercise the padded scale in a
real GEMM2 call on this
model until #21397 is also fixed — not a coincidence of which crash I
hit first, a property of
`moe_intermediate_size=2304` / `group_size=32`. The fix is not
model-specific, though: a
different W4A8-MXFP4 MoE model whose `moe_intermediate_size` doesn't
share this 64/32
relationship could hit the odd-group crash without #21397's constraint,
and would exercise this
code path for real.

So: confirmed correct for the crash it targets (unit test + real
hardware), but end-to-end
correctness of the padded scale inside the actual down_proj GEMM remains
unverified and, for
this specific model, unverifiable until #21397 is resolved too. Flagging
for reviewers rather
than claiming full correctness.

Fixes #21396

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's W4A8-MXFP4 MoE weight loading no longer
crashes when a TP shard
leaves an odd scale-group count. A release-note fragment is included
(release_notes/fragments/21399.yaml).

### How was this patch tested?

- Added
`tests/ut/quantization/methods/w4a8/test_w4a8_mxfp4.py::TestAscendW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod::test_process_weights_pads_odd_tp_scale_groups`,
covering a `(8, 128, 9)` scale shard; confirmed it reproduces the exact
crash
(`RuntimeError: shape '[8, 128, 4, 2]' is invalid for input of size
9216`) against the
unpatched code, and passes with the fix. Also added a round-trip check
that
`restore_weights_for_rl_loading` drops the padding correctly instead of
crashing (caught by
Gemini Code Assist's review — the first version of this fix only handled
the forward
  direction).
- Ran the full `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w4a8/test_w4a8_mxfp4.py`
suite (24 tests) — all pass.
- Verified on real A5 hardware (TP=8, native FP8
`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` checkpoint): this
fix clears the reshape crash and weight loading completes (see caveat
above for what's not
  yet verified beyond that).
- `git diff --check`, `codespell`, and `ruff` (matching the repo's
pinned `v0.14.0`) pass on
  the changed files.

Documentation only. Add the user guide and release note for the combined

documentation PR.

1. Compared the extracted guide with #20485 and checked its options and
restrictions against the framework configuration validation.

format.sh ci` was attempted, but actionlint environment installation
timed out after 300 seconds.

are recorded in #22045.

+## Experimental Qwen GDN RecoverSSM
+
+Qwen GDN hybrid models like Qwen3.5/3.6 can use experimental RecoverSSM on
+Ascend A3 and A5. For Qwen3.8, use the Qwen3.5-compatible dense checkpoint
+`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`.
+
+Enable this path with `--use-replayssm`, which is off by default. Use Model
+Runner V2 with [MTP](#speculating-using-mtp), [DSpark](#speculating-using-dspark),
+or [DFlash](#speculating-using-dflash) and a speculative window appropriate for
+your checkpoint and draft model.
+
+For example, run Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with DFlash speculative config mode:
+
+```shell
+--use-replayssm \
+--speculative-config '{"method": "DFlash", "model": "/path/to/dflash", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
+```
+
+Use BF16 activations and convolution state, and BF16 or FP32 SSM checkpoints.
+Set PP, PCP, and DCP to 1. The TP size must divide both the key-head
+and value-head counts, and the value-head count must be a multiple of the
+key-head count. Disable stochastic rounding. Ascend 310P is unsupported.
+
+Use `--mamba-cache-mode none --no-enable-prefix-caching` with prefix caching
+disabled, or `--mamba-cache-mode align --enable-prefix-caching` to enable it.
+In `align` mode, the Mamba block size must cover at least
+`num_speculative_tokens + 1` tokens.
+
+For direct prefill-to-decode transfer, use `MooncakePullConnector` or
+`MooncakeConnectorV2` with its default pull mode (`use_layerwise=false`).
+Enable `--use-replayssm` on both roles and match the model weights, TP size,
+speculative method, draft checkpoint where applicable, speculative window,
+state dtypes, convolution layout, and prefix-caching configuration.
+
+For example, use these settings for a same-host TP4 + TP4 deployment with
+Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MTP with four speculative tokens, and prefix caching:
+
+| Setting | Prefill | Decode |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Tensor parallel size | 4 | 4 |
+| KV role | `kv_producer` | `kv_consumer` |
+| SSM checkpoint dtype | `float32` | `float32` |
+| Mamba cache mode | `align` | `align` |
+| Prefix caching | Enabled | Enabled |
+
+For Mooncake transport setup and request routing, see
+[Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (DeepSeek)](../../tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.md).
+
+The Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MTP generation test checks completion and token validity
+with RecoverSSM off and on in eager and graph-enabled configurations, including
+repeated requests in `none` and `align` modes. The Qwen3.8-27B operator cases

In this mode each draft token at position `i` is accepted with a configured probability `rates[i]`, compared against a uniform random draw — **independent of the target/draft probability match**. [Test] Adapt fused copy-SFA nightly tests to runner-owned stable prefixes (#20289) (#23018)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#20289 (delayed D2H) changed fused copy-SFA metadata geometry to read
per-request
stable prefixes from
`common_attn_metadata.req_topk_buffer_stable_prefixes`
  instead of deriving them from `seq_lens`
  (vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_kv_offload.py).

The nightly singlecard_ops fixture builds its `common_attn_metadata` as
a
  SimpleNamespace without the new field, so all 24 cases in

`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention.py`
  fail on the A3/A5 nightlies with:
  This PR adapts the fixture:

- add `req_topk_buffer_stable_prefixes` to `common()`, aligned to
`seq_lens`
rounded down to complete 128-token blocks (the runner's
retired-full-block
    semantics)
- refresh the tensor wherever tests mutate `seq_lens` in place,
preserving the
    rollback / hot-budget lifecycle intent of those cases
- recompute prefix/logical/tail/ring/reuse assertions under the new
geometry
    (e.g. seq 10371 now maps to prefix 10368, logical 8195)

  ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

  No — test-only adaptation.

  ### How was this patch tested?

- ruff check / ruff format / py_compile pass locally (py312, matching CI
pins).
- Assertion values were recomputed from the production geometry formulas
in
`vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_kv_offload.py`
(prefix/cache/logical/tail/ring).
- A3/A5 nightly on this branch is the final gate; in the 2026-11-23
nightly
logs all 24 failures per platform were the same AttributeError with no
    assertion mismatches.

[Feature][SpecDecode] Enable GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 graph in PD serving (#22172)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 speculative decoding to use FA3 and ACL
Graph in both single-node PD-mixed and two-node PD-disaggregated
serving. This extends the basic DFlash2 support added by #21439.

The change:

- allows supported GLM DFlash2 local drafts to select FA3 without
requiring `enforce_eager=true`;
- keeps common FA3 capability checks active while separating
target-global PP/PCP/DCP and C8 restrictions behind an explicit
local-draft exception;
- preserves the physical `BLHNC/HND/LBHNC` KV-cache layouts while
exposing the zero-copy logical `[page, token, head, dim]` FA3 view;
- safely falls back when the target text config, live loader tag, draft
architecture, dtype, selector capability, hardware, or FA3 operator is
unsupported;
- does not introduce new environment variables, public APIs, or
release-note YAML files.

The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`. The overlap with the
already merged #22159 is resolved by retaining its generic FA3 scheduler
initialization and HND cache fixes, then applying this PR's graph-draft
eligibility and `BLHNC` support on top.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Supported GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 deployments can use
`enforce_eager=false` with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`; target and DFlash2 draft
graphs are captured independently. Unsupported configurations keep their
previous backend selection.

### How was this patch tested?

Validated on Ascend A3 with `GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8-1013` and
`GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2`.

The single-node PD-mixed configuration uses one 16-card process group
with `DP8/TP2`, one API endpoint, and no proxy. The two-node
PD-disaggregated configuration uses `DP2/TP8/PCP1` in Prefill and
`DP8/TP2/PCP1` in Decode, with a load-balancing proxy. All serving roles
use `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with `enforce_eager=false`; both the target and
DFlash2 draft capture FULL graphs. Decode consumes the KV cache
transferred by Prefill through the existing disaggregated KV path.

MTP uses `method=deepseek_mtp, num_speculative_tokens=3`. DFlash2 uses
`method=dflash, num_speculative_tokens=7`. Because K differs, these
results compare the intended production configurations rather than
equal-K algorithm efficiency.

#### Full GSM8K: single-node PD-mixed

All 1319 GSM8K questions were evaluated with the 4-shot CoT chat prompt,
greedy decoding, batch size 16, maximum output 8192, and no accuracy
warmup. Accuracy, acceptance metrics, and performance metrics below come
from the same inference run.

| Metric | MTP K=3 | DFlash2 K=7 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Correct / total | 1290 / 1319 | 1280 / 1319 |
| Accuracy | 97.8014% | 97.0432% |
| Draft acceptance | 83.3758% | 64.9477% |
| Acceptance length incl. target | 3.5013 | 5.5463 |
| TTFT | 623.14 ms | 701.42 ms |
| TPOT | 30.645 ms | 26.975 ms |
| ITL | 106.066 ms | 151.537 ms |
| ITL/TPOT | 3.461 | 5.618 |
| Output token/s | 437.17 | 515.16 |

All 1319 requests completed successfully with zero preemptions. For
DFlash2, the same evaluator returned 1279/1319 before numeric
normalization and 1280/1319 after correcting the GSM8K
thousands-separator parsing issue.

#### Full GSM8K: two-node PD-disaggregated

All 1319 GSM8K questions were evaluated with the same prompt, sampling,
batch size, and maximum output limit. Accuracy, acceptance metrics, and
performance metrics below come from the same inference run.

| Metric | MTP K=3 | DFlash2 K=7 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Correct / total | 1281 / 1319 | 1284 / 1319 |
| Accuracy | 97.1190% | 97.3465% |
| Draft acceptance | 81.7340% | 63.8422% |
| Acceptance length incl. target | 3.4520 | 5.4690 |
| TTFT | 289.218 ms | 296.261 ms |
| TPOT | 11.536 ms | 8.117 ms |
| ITL | 40.445 ms | 45.668 ms |
| ITL/TPOT | 3.506 | 5.626 |
| Output token/s | 862.16 | 1286.94 |

All 1319 requests completed successfully with zero preemptions.

#### Functional and regression coverage

- A3 logs confirm target and DFlash2 draft FULL graph capture in both
deployment modes.
- Focused unit tests on the rebased branch cover local-draft routing,
physical KV-cache layout consistency, zero-copy FA3 views, and
unsupported configuration fallback.
- Changed files: `vllm_ascend/platform.py`,
`vllm_ascend/attention/flash_attention_v3.py`, and three focused
attention unit-test files.


- vLLM main:

[Misc][KV Transfer] Report Mooncake delayed-free status from the sending thread (#22422)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Mooncake's producer control thread can receive a completion notification
and
queue a request for release while the scheduler's drain path is idle
(engine on
0-token steps / the connector gate closed). A small DEBUG-only queue
snapshot
makes pending releases visible during that idle period.

This revision follows the minimal observation design proposed in review
(`wangxiaoteng888/vllm-ascend#6`): a DEBUG-only pending-release sample
instead of
a stalled-drain verdict. The production diff adds 23 lines in
`pull_scheduler.py`:

- Check `logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)` before invoking the
reporter from
  the existing sending loop.
- At most once per 10 seconds, sample `finished_requests.qsize()` and
log a
nonzero count as `Mooncake delayed-free status: engine_id=...
pending_release=...`.
- Catch observation errors so normal control-message processing can
continue.

The scheduler drain method, DONE handling, heartbeat handling and lease
expiry
logic remain exactly as they were on the baseline. The observer does not
acquire
`state_lock`, track a cross-thread drain flag, scan leases, consume the
queue, or
release blocks. DEBUG disabled skips the reporter entirely; a log-level
check per
control-loop iteration and one initialized timestamp field remain. This
is not a
claim of literally zero overhead or a measured performance improvement.

The release-chain blind spot itself is unchanged: blocks are still
released only
by the drain path (that fix is vllm-ascend#21918). This PR adds
observation only.

### Reading the diagnostic

Enable DEBUG logging on P with the existing launch configuration, run a
small PD
workload, stop new arrivals and keep P/D running. Correlate repeated
`pending_release` samples with P-side `reason=done
action=queued_for_release` and
`Finished sending KV transfer` logs.

The reported queue size is a concurrent snapshot. It does not measure
request age
or count drain operations. The same count in multiple samples can
represent
different requests. A single line, or an unchanged count under ongoing
traffic,
is not proof of a stalled drain. No line means no nonzero queue was
sampled while
logging and the control thread were active; it is not proof of system
health.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

One DEBUG-only diagnostic; no new configuration and no changes to
transfer/release semantics. No release note fragment is included for
this
logging-only change (precedent: vllm-ascend#22643).

### How was this patch tested?

- Four source-isolated CPU repository test cases pass: the DEBUG
disabled/enabled control-loop paths (disabled must not read the clock or
sample
the queue), cadence plus read-only sampling (including an expired lease
left
for the normal drain path, with the bookkeeping snapshot unchanged), and
an
  observation failure that keeps the control loop serving.
- The tests use a logger with its own `logging.Manager`, so a global
`logging.disable()` left behind by another test cannot silence the
sample; this
was confirmed against the local CPU suite where the whole `tests/ut`
tree runs
  in one process.
- `tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_pull_scheduler.py`: 139 passed /
4 failed
  locally, i.e. the same 4 pre-existing pin artifacts as the baseline
(an upstream test calls `get_request_block_hasher` with three arguments
while
  the local vLLM pin still takes two).
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean for both changed files.

NPU inference accuracy, end-to-end performance, and the CI matrix itself
are left
to the pipeline run on this commit.

### Checklist

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: DEBUG-off path, empty queue,
expired
  lease present, and observation error are covered.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: a failing sample is logged and
the
  control loop keeps serving DONE and heartbeat traffic.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: assertions check the actual call
counts of
  the clock and queue sampling, not just log text.
- [x] **Performance impact**: DEBUG-off pays one log-level check per
loop
iteration and no clock read or sampling; DEBUG-on samples once per 10s.

[BugFix] Construct the Qwen4Exp PLE once with prefill context parallelism (#22942)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

During Qwen4Exp initialization with PCP enabled, the decoder builds a
base PLE, allocates its host embedding table and registers it. The
Ascend backbone then deletes the registration and constructs a PCP PLE
for the same layer. This repeats the allocation and registration even on
a single DP replica.

Choose the backend when the upstream decoder constructs each PLE. With
PCP > 1, each worker constructs one Ascend PCP PLE per local PLE layer,
regardless of DP size. With PCP = 1 it constructs one base PLE. The
decoder and the static forward context reference the same instance
throughout initialization. The existing upstream module binding reads
the parallel config for each construction. An upstream PLE
class-selection hook could replace that binding.

Follows #21693. Supersedes #22922.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Qwen4Exp PCP deployments avoid the redundant initialization
automatically. Existing requirements for supported PCP topologies still
apply.

### How was this patch tested?

- Six constructor and registration regression cases passed. Applying the
same tests to the previous PR head reproduced the extra constructor for
DP1/PCP2 and DP1/PCP4.
- Four Ascend 950 devices, real Qwen weights, PP1. Tested DP/TP/PCP
1/2/2, 2/1/2 and 2/2/1. A constructor probe recorded one instance per
local PLE layer on every worker and checked the class and object
identity in the static forward context. PCP4 coverage is limited to the
constructor regression test.
- Each topology served 320 unique 16,384-token requests at concurrency
64 and 80 unique 131,072-token requests at concurrency 8, with one
output token per request. All completed successfully. These are
functional and initialization checks. Peak memory and throughput changes
were not measured.
- The device image used its existing GDN implementation via an import
compatibility shim. The TP1 topology used the previously validated A5
multi-KV-head attention adapter for long inputs. The model source
SHA-256 on every worker matched the tested working copy at 579888dbe.
After rebasing on upstream 15697aa82, the only difference in the tested
model file is the upstream GDN import relocation to
vllm_ascend.attention.gdn. The PLE changes and regression test are
identical.
- Ruff 0.14.0 lint and format checks passed on both changed files.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage
- [x] Regression test
- [ ] Error / failure path coverage
- [x] Meaningful and reliable tests
- [ ] Performance benchmark

[Performance][EPLB] Optimize expert mapping and load recording (#17579)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

In Model Runner V2, EPLB maps each token’s top-k logical expert IDs to
physical experts and records how many tokens each local expert
processed. On main, the map kernel uses a fixed tile of 256 assignments
for both decode and prefill, and the record kernel handles all local
experts in one Triton program.

This PR selects the map tile size from the number of assignments. Small
decode batches can spread work across more cores, while large prefills
process more assignments per tile. The kernel specializes on top-k and
keeps the assignment count dynamic, so batches within a tile size can
reuse a compiled variant. For load recording, each program handles up to
256 local experts, allowing larger expert sets to run across multiple
programs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The V2 MoE factory registers map warmup for EPLB-enabled routers when
`kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup` is enabled. The existing configuration
and operator interfaces are unchanged. [Release
note](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/108738ac2d243cfb9bc266b3d85d8ebacab7555f/release_notes/fragments/17579.yaml)

### How was this patch tested?

#### A3 model results against main

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash W8A8 ran on a single A3 node with DP2/TP8/EP16, full
decode graph replay and asynchronous EPLB (window 200, interval 300).
Both versions served the full GSM8K test split at concurrency 16 with
the same zero-shot prompts and greedy decoding. Each version ran one
timed pass after warmup.

| GSM8K metric | PR change vs main |
| --- | ---: |
| Output throughput | **+7.36%** |
| Request throughput | +7.51% |
| Total serving time | −6.98% |
| End-to-end latency P50 / P95 | −0.79% / −8.99% |
| Time to first token P50 / P95 | +0.26% / +5.15% |
| Inter-token latency P50 / P95 | −1.35% / −2.78% |

| GSM8K exact-match accuracy | Main | PR |

| Timed run | 96.06% | 95.91% |
| Separate accuracy run | 95.91% | 96.06% |

two concurrent requests of 16,384 input and 1,024 output tokens each.

| Pure-decode metric | PR change vs main, P50 / P95 |

| Map device duration | −74.09% / −70.93% |

#### Operator results against main

The map and record kernels were validated at `b7ac9d60` with CANN 9.2.1

reference exactly in eager execution and Graph replay. Map speedups
